SECANT PILING

Secant Piling: A Client’s Guide to the Right Starting Questions

Understand the decisions behind a secant pile wall before requesting a price.

In this insight

Start with the excavation briefDescribe the boundaries, not just the depthCompare the complete work packageRequest evidence that supports a decisionFor your project discussionDiscuss a project ↗

Educational overview · Project-specific design and execution require qualified review.

Start with the excavation brief

A secant pile wall uses intersecting piles to create an earth-retaining barrier. That description is simple; the commercial brief rarely is. A developer may need basement space, a main contractor may need a buildable sequence, and a designer may need reliable information about ground and neighbouring assets. Begin by agreeing which problem the wall must solve. An early brief should distinguish retention, groundwater management and any intended permanent structural role.

Describe the boundaries, not just the depth

A useful enquiry includes site boundaries, proposed excavation levels, available investigation reports, nearby structures and access restrictions. State whether the internal layout is fixed or still evolving. A later change in basement geometry can affect wall length, support positions and working space. Mark unknowns explicitly so a bidder can explain assumptions rather than quietly filling information gaps with a different interpretation.

Compare the complete work package

Ask what is included beyond drilling and concrete. Setting out, working-platform provision, spoil handling, testing, wall trimming, support interfaces and records can sit in different packages. The cheapest pile rate may therefore describe the smallest scope. A comparison schedule should place each inclusion beside its responsible party and delivery date. This makes scope gaps visible while they can still be resolved commercially.

Request evidence that supports a decision

A credible proposal should explain the planned approach, the information still needed and the approval route. Ask for relevant personnel, proposed equipment and an example of installation records. Avoid using an impressive machine photograph as a substitute for project-specific planning. Treat any early programme as conditional on the stated access, ground information, approvals and supply assumptions; the next useful output is a coordinated feasibility discussion.

For your project discussion

Use these questions to structure a conversation with the project’s qualified design and delivery team. This article is general procurement guidance, not a site-specific design, method statement or compliance assessment. The cited international resources provide background; applicable local requirements and the approved project documents govern the work.

Take this into your next conversation

  • Issue one shared ground-information pack.
  • Separate wall scope from excavation and support interfaces.
  • Compare assumptions before comparing rates.
